subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Human life will be prolonged by a new drug called new-med.

options.text: A new drug called new-med was prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.
A new drug called new-med is prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med had prolonged human life.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of the sentence is **declarative** and the tense of the given sentence is **future simple**.
 
• The **subject **of the given **passive **sentence is **"human life"** and the **object **is **"a new drug called new-med".**
 
• The format of passive voice for future simple tense is: **Subject + will be + V3 (past participle form of the verb) + by + Object.**
 
• The format of active voice for future simple tense is: **Subject (Objective case)+ will + V1 (base form of the verb) + object (Subjective case).**
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• "A new planet will be discovered by the scientists." (Passive Voice)
 
• "The scientist will discover a new planet." (Active Voice)
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- “A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 ("A new drug called new-med was prolonging human life."**) uses the past continuous tense, which does not match the future intention of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3 ("A new drug called new-med is prolonging human life.") **is in the present continuous tense, which does not accurately represent the future action implied in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("A new drug called new-med had prolonged human life.") **uses the past perfect tense, which is incorrect because the sentence is about a future event, not a completed action in the past.
